newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S KWV TO PROBE CHAMPAGNE FRAUD CHARGES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S KWV TO PROBE CHAMPAGNE FRAUD CHARGES.

text.p: South Africa's KWV wine cooperative said on Thursday it had begun a probe into allegations that it passed off its products as French-made champagne during the 1980s.

A statement said the cooperative, once South Africa's premier wine exporter, was being accused of having had a part in a scheme to disguise the true origin of its products during the years of anti-apartheid sanctions.

"It appears that the price-quality ratio of KWV's products left considerable room for other parties during the sanctions period to purchase these products legally and then to make new or amended claims of origin elsewhere to suit the target market," the statement said.
"New allegations now also indicate that KWV could possibly have assisted such an agent to label products on his behalf in a manner which concealed its South African identity," it said.
Last week local newspapers quoted documents leaked by an undisclosed source as saying KWV employees had taken part in a scheme to sell products of the cooperative as French champagne.
Only sparkling wine produced in the Champagne region of France according to an approved method may be sold as champagne.
KWV is locked in a row with Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom, who has forced the cooperative to delay its plans to convert to a private company.

Hanekom has said he wants more time to study, among other things, whether KWV assets were acquired due to its role as statutory regulator of the wine industry and should therefore belong to the state.

The KWV statement said the cooperative's board "would do everything in its power to obtain full details with regard to allegations that the organisation had been involved in an illegal transaction during the 1980s".

"This decision has been taken in the long-term interest of KWV, its members and the South African wine industry," it said. "The internal investigation will be conducted at the highest level and with the greatest degree of urgency."
